papers.title_en: NavCMPO: Critic-Guided MeanFlow Policy Optimization for Adaptive Navigation
papers.authors: Junjie An, Yi Wu, Xiao Liu, Yiqun Zhou, Yuechen Wu, Xiaoqing Guan, You Wang, Guang Li
papers.evidence: 使用强化学习微调进行自适应导航路径规划
papers.tldr: 现有端到端扩散导航策略推理延迟高且依赖专家演示质量。NavCMPO提出两阶段框架，使用少步MeanFlow生成轨迹，结合评论家引导细化与强化学习微调。在InternVLA-N1基准上，平均成功率74.7%，比NavDP基线高6.4%，推理延迟从85ms降至60ms。该方法有效平衡了速度与避障能力，并实现sim-to-real迁移。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end diffusion-based policies have demonstrated strong performance in mapless visual navigation, but their iterative denoising process introduces substantial inference latency, while behavior cloning limits performance to the quality of expert demonstrations. We present NavCMPO, a two-stage adaptive navigation framework that combines few-step MeanFlow trajectory generation, critic-guided refinement, and reinforcement learning fine-tuning. During pre-training, an obstacle proximity prediction task encourages the visual representation to capture obstacle-aware spatial information. To compensate for the degradation in obstacle avoidance caused by few-step generation, Critic-Guided Trajectory Refinement (CGTR) uses gradients from a critic trained with obstacle-point-cloud supervision to refine intermediate trajectories. During adaptation, the MeanFlow policy is fine-tuned using Proximal Policy Optimization with behavior-cloning regularization, while the critic is updated to accommodate embodiment-specific observation changes. Under a matched training budget on the InternVLA-N1 benchmark, NavCMPO achieves an average success rate of 74.7\%, exceeding the retrained NavDP baseline by 6.4 percentage points, while reducing inference latency from 85\,ms to 60\,ms. Experiments on a Unitree Go2 further demonstrate effective sim-to-real transfer.

papers.title_en: Difference-Based Relational Learning for Zero-Shot Object-Goal Visual Navigation With Direct Sim-to-Real Transfer
papers.evidence: 深度强化学习用于机器人路径规划
papers.tldr: 零样本物体目标视觉导航面临物体外观变化和窄视场角导致的仿真-现实差距。本文提出T-DRN，利用孪生网络提取目标与观测物体的关系差异，获得领域无关特征；并采用双帧时间缓冲保持短时物体连续性。在AI2-THOR仿真中T-DRN提升了零样本泛化的成功率。进一步在物理轮式机器人上验证了直接仿真到现实迁移的鲁棒性，证明了方法的实用性。
papers.abstract_en: End-to-end deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for zero-shot object-goal visual navigation remains challenged by the sim-to-real gap, particularly variations in object appearance and restricted camera field-of-view (FoV). This letter proposes a Temporal Difference-Relational Network (T-DRN) for robust zero-shot sim-to-real transfer. T-DRN combines a Siamese difference-based feature extractor, which computes relational difference between the target and observed objects to produce domain-independent representations, with a dual-frame temporal buffer that preserves short-term object continuity under narrow FoV. Extensive experiments in AI2-THOR demonstrate that T-DRN improves zero-shot generalization in terms of success rates over strong baselines. Furthermore, T-DRN is systematically validated on a physical wheeled robot, demonstrating robust performance under real sensing and actuation constraints and supporting the feasibility of direct sim-to-real transfer.
